summary: Bounded review of the unchanged proposed rules only; live release unknown. Participant/identity/ownership and create/update protections pass 14 emulator groups. Public-location publication and abuse prevention remain release concerns.

findings.issue: Preserved prayer/feast rules allow public document reads and precise coordinates; publication consent and rounding are not server-enforced. The deployed rules and historical consent are unverified.
findings.recommendation: Obtain the active rules export, review historical consent/data, and design approved trusted minimization and auditable publication consent without assuming client display rounding is access control.

findings.issue: Invitation creation/message writes have identity/schema checks but no per-user rate policy or blocking. Existing reporting is study-scoped. Community expansion could expose recipients to abuse.
findings.recommendation: Define backend-enforced rate/block/report controls as separately reviewed work before community expansion; retain participant-only private message access.

findings.issue: Client rules do not constrain privileged Admin SDK/IAM access; the actual project access policy and active rules release have not been inspected.
findings.recommendation: Require administrator release export, IAM/service-account review and retention/access policy evidence; do not infer production privacy from emulator success.
